newsitem.title: MEXICO: Leftist party says it can prove Mexico vote fraud.
newsitem.headline: Leftist party says it can prove Mexico vote fraud.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist party on Tuesday showed what it claimed was documented proof of electoral fraud that may have swung the governor's race to the ruling party in the southeastern state of Campeche.
The alleged fraud took place during July 6 elections, when opposition parties made historic gains against the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has ruled Mexico for 68 years.
Despite the strong opposition showing, the PRI held on to the statehouse in Campeche, a sparsely populated and backward state on the Yucatan Peninsula.
The leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) said it had enough evidence for elections officials to declare the election void.
"The election in Campeche was not fair, not legal, not transparent," Amalia Garcia, a party leader in charge of the PRD's Campeche investigation, told a news conference.
PRD leaders held up what it claimed were falsified ballots that were among 24,000 created by the PRI.
The PRI's governor-elect of Campeche, Antonio Gonzalez Curi, defeated second-place candidate Layda Sansores of the PRD by 15,351 votes, taking 108,249 votes to Sansores' 92,898.

The July 6 elections were hailed as the cleanest in Mexico's checkered political history, as opposition parties posted landmark gains that saw the PRI lose its majority in the lower house of Congress for the first time.
The PRI, the party with the longest period of uninterrupted rule in the world, has historically kept office through a combination of populism, patronage and alleged fraud.
PRD leaders said that despite the democratic advances in the recent elections, the PRI had used fraud in places like Campeche.

The PRD said that in addition to falsifying ballots, the PRI also overspent well beyond the legal limit of 4.8 million pesos (about $615,000) by spending more than 40 million pesos (about $5.1 million).
